dedupe_keys.name: municipal heat planning data nrw kommunale warmeplanung nrw building heat demand heat lines scenarios and heat potentials

description: The North Rhine-Westphalia environment agency LANUK publishes data packages to support municipal heat planning, prepared within its potential study on future heat supply in NRW and extended continuously as parts are finished. Space heating and hot water demand of residential and non-residential buildings was recalculated for the 2024 model, with projections under three renovation scenarios for 2025, 2030, 2035, 2040 and 2045, at building level and per street segment as heat lines, which also include process heat demand of commerce and services at temperatures suited to heat networks; each building carries a building type and age class, based on the summer 2022 LoD1 and LoD2 building model. Further data give modernisation potentials, likelihood of implementation and heating fuels used, by building block and parcel district from property listings and InWIS models, together with potentials from the study, such as ground-mounted solar thermal by parcel district from DWD radiation data. Data come as a shapefile per municipality and an NRW-wide Esri geodatabase, with a short PDF on sources and methods and an Excel table of attribute columns; the entry was updated on 14 September 2026. Coverage is North Rhine-Westphalia. Data are free under the Data Licence Germany Zero 2.0. Caveats: the agency warns of large deviations for single buildings, so buildings should be aggregated, and theoretical potentials far exceed demand before local screening. Simulation uses are heat demand mapping and district heating network planning and decarbonisation scenarios. Related records: data-hamburg-gas-hydrogen-network-heat-planning covers Hamburg.
